description.text: At Twist Bioscience Corporation, we work in service of our customers who are changing the world for the better. In fields such as health care, food/agriculture, industrial chemicals/materials and academic research, by using our products, our customers are developing ways to better lives and improve the sustainability of the planet. We believe Twist Bioscience is uniquely positioned to help accelerate their efforts and the faster our customers succeed, the better for all of us. We have developed a disruptive DNA synthesis platform to industrialize the engineering of biology. The core of our platform is a proprietary technology that pioneers a new method of manufacturing synthetic DNA by “writing” DNA on a silicon chip. We have miniaturized traditional chemical DNA synthesis reactions to write over 1,000,000 pieces of DNA (oligonucleotides) up to 500 bases through direct synthesis on each silicon chip, approximately the size of a large mobile phone, reducing by 99.8% the amount of chemicals we estimate would be used per gene as compared to plate-based synthesis. We have combined our silicon-based DNA writing technology with proprietary software, scalable commercial infrastructure and an e-commerce platform to create an integrated technology platform that enables us to achieve high levels of quality, precision, automation, and manufacturing throughput at a significantly lower cost and quicker than our competitors.

about.description_short: At Twist Bioscience, our customizable solutions across the biological continuum raise the bar in diagnostics, therapeutics, industrial, agriculture and research markets. We drive innovation with confidence, without compromise. Whether delivering oligos, genes, proteins, libraries, characterization data, antibody discovery solutions, or NGS workflow tools, our scientific expertise and exceptional customer experience help navigate complex challenges, all with precision and at the scale and speed customers require. By enhancing R&D efficiency at every turn, we give scientists more shots on goal - more experiments, more iterations, more chances for remarkable discoveries. Together, we stand with customers in the relentless pursuit of progress, backed by enterprise reliability, to shape a healthier and more sustainable future for all.

# TWST — Twist Bioscience Corporation
v5 run, 2026-10-19. **In scope** (market cap $7.940B at $132.75, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B scope cap). US filer on Form 10-K (FY2025, period ended 2025-09-30). No overrides — no DATA_GAP fired on the preliminary or final run.

All valuation figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Operating metrics for periods after FY2025 (customer count, segment growth, quarterly prints, guidance) are as reported in the company's Q3 FY2026 earnings release.

## What it is
Synthetic-DNA manufacturer on a proprietary silicon-chip synthesis platform, in two businesses: DNA Synthesis & Protein Solutions (clonal genes, oligo pools, variant libraries, antibody/protein solutions for drug discovery) and NGS Applications (target-enrichment panels and library-prep kits for sequencing). Customers are research labs, biotech/pharma drug developers, diagnostics, agriculture and industrial users — ~2,650 customers in Q3 FY2026, with demand increasingly tied to AI-enabled drug discovery (therapeutics revenue +49% YoY in Q3 FY2026; an antibody-characterization collaboration feeding Eli Lilly's TuneLab AI platform).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow -$47,628,000; capex $28,004,000; SBC $64,459,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: -$140,091,000 = $-2.34/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-2.34, latest FY OE total $-140.1M, shares diluted 59,808,000). FCF was -$75,632,000 before SBC — the cash burn is not an SBC artifact alone.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): -$86,727,000 for FY2025 in financials_history.csv — same sign, smaller magnitude; the conservative OCF-based figure is the scored series.
- OE positive **0 of the last 5** fiscal years (key_numbers.md: 0/5). Per-year conservative OE/share from financials_history.csv: FY2023 -$3.53, FY2024 -$2.07, FY2025 -$2.34 — no improving per-share trend in the scored window despite revenue growth, because SBC rose from $30,278,000 (FY2023) to $50,925,000 (FY2024) to $64,459,000 (FY2025).
- **Base used = TTM OE/share $-2.59** (base_source: ttm_json; key_numbers.md). FY2025 ended 2025-09-30, thirteen months before this run (STALE_FY), so the final run pins the TTM base per WORKER_SPEC step 4 — the ttm.json legs are quoted in the next bullet. The normalized 3-yr median is $-2.34/share and the latest FY is also $-2.34/share (key_numbers.md): negative on every basis, so the tier is F whichever base is used; the pinned TTM base is also the more conservative of the two.
- **TTM legs (ttm.py, through Q3 FY2026 / 2026-06-30):** OCF FY -$47,628,000 − prior YTD -$35,814,000 + current YTD -$41,258,000 = **TTM -$53,072,000**; capex FY $28,004,000 − prior YTD $15,577,000 + current YTD $27,624,000 = **TTM $40,051,000**; SBC FY $64,459,000 − prior YTD $48,376,000 + current YTD $50,385,000 = **TTM $66,468,000**; shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) **61,726,000**. **TTM OE total -$159,591,000 → TTM OE/share -$2.59.** This TTM figure is the scored base (see above).
- Balance sheet (latest FY, financials_history.csv / fundamentals.json): cash $183,049,000 plus short-term investments $49,385,000; total assets $641,861,000; total liabilities $168,903,000; book equity $472,958,000; PPE net $102,283,000; operating lease liabilities $75,572,000; current ratio 3.64 (fundamentals.json). No funded-debt tag reports for FY2025 — see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK under Flags.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, platform real, economics unproven
Justification: Silicon-chip DNA synthesis platform with real scale and process leverage — revenue $245.1M → $313.0M → $376.6M (FY2023-25) and gross margin over the last five fiscal years of 39.1% (FY2021) → 41.4% (FY2022) → 36.6% (FY2023) → 42.6% (FY2024) → 50.7% (FY2025) (fundamentals.json), 52.8% in Q3 FY2026 — but no demonstrated return on capital: roic_proxy is deeply negative in every one of the last five years (-103.5% FY2021, -45.2% FY2022, -50.9% FY2023, -70.8% FY2024, -37.1% FY2025 in fundamentals.json) and conservative owner's earnings are positive in 0 of the last 5 years, so there is no ROIC history above the cost of capital to support a 7+. Competition is from far larger tools companies (IDT/Danaher, GenScript, Agilent, Illumina) plus benchtop enzymatic challengers, and SBC of $64.5M in FY2025 (~17% of revenue) keeps diluting holders at 3.5%/yr. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
- FOR: Proprietary silicon-based DNA synthesis platform: high-throughput, miniaturized synthesis gives a structural cost/throughput position in genes and oligo pools that traditional column synthesis cannot match at scale; Scale and share gains in the numbers: revenue $245.1M (FY2023) → $313.0M (FY2024) → $376.6M (FY2025), 14 consecutive quarters of sequential growth through Q3 FY2026, ~2,650 customers in Q3 FY2026; Gross margin expansion evidencing process leverage: 36.6% (FY2023) → 42.6% (FY2024) → 50.7% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json, 52.8% in Q3 FY2026; Embedded workflow position across both segments — DNA Synthesis & Protein Solutions and NGS Applications (target-enrichment panels) — with AI-driven drug-discovery demand (therapeutics revenue +49% YoY in Q3 FY2026; Lilly TuneLab collaboration).
- AGAINST: No demonstrated returns on capital: owner's earnings positive in 0 of the last 5 years, roic_proxy deeply negative in fundamentals.json (-50.9% FY2023, -70.8% FY2024, -37.1% FY2025) — the franchise has never earned above its cost of capital; Giant, well-funded rivals on every line: IDT (Danaher) in oligos/synthesis, GenScript and Azenta GeneWiz in gene synthesis, Agilent and Illumina in NGS enrichment — plus enzymatic benchtop synthesis (DNA Script, Telesis Bio) threatening the centralized model; SBC is a heavy and rising real cost: $30.3M (FY2023) → $50.9M (FY2024) → $64.5M (FY2025) → $66.5M TTM, ~17% of FY2025 revenue; diluted share count up 3.5%/yr (53.9M FY2022 → 59.8M FY2025 → 61.7M TTM); Customer and funding concentration: NGS top-10 accounts are a large share of that segment's revenue and many customers are VC-funded biotechs whose demand depends on the biotech funding cycle; Operating leverage unproven: SG&A was ~66% of FY2025 revenue in the filed statements and the operating loss was still $136.3M on $376.6M of revenue.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. (Moot for the score — see DCF.)

## DCF — Tier F: no scenario table exists, and that is the finding
The engine's Tier F branch fired: neither the pinned TTM base (-$2.59/share) nor the normalized median (-$2.34/share) is positive, so no scenarios, IVs, or IRRs are computed (implied_irr_weighted: null in dcf_numbers.json). Probabilities recorded for the run: 10/25/30/25/10 (defaults — nothing in the evidence justifies tilting weights for a branch that does not use them).
- **F sub-type: no_cash_generation** (f_subtype_basis: ttm.json legs under the TTM pin — TTM OCF -$53,072,000 minus TTM capex $40,051,000 is negative before SBC). The annual window agrees: FCF legs from financials_history.csv are FY2023 -$170,253,000, FY2024 -$69,170,000, FY2025 -$75,632,000 — OCF − capex is negative in every year of the window before SBC is even deducted. This is genuine cash burn, not the "SBC ate positive FCF" subtype.
- **Growth sanity check:** the engine's blend is 19.22% (key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 33.12%, rev CAGR 3y 22.75%, latest rev YoY 20.32%). The default-offset scenario starts the blend implies (7.2% / 14.2% / 19.2% / 24.2% / 31.2%) are plausible against the prints — Q3 FY2026 revenue +23% YoY ($118.4M) and FY2026 guidance of $456–457M (~+21% vs FY2025 revenue of $376,572,000) bracket the base start, and the super-bull start of 31.2% sits below the 5-yr CAGR of 33.12%. No recalibration is needed — and decisively, growth applied to a negative base produces no valuation in any case. No growth input changes this tier.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 13 months ago): resolved by running ttm.py and pinning the TTM base in the final run (--ttm, per WORKER_SPEC step 4) — the TTM legs are quoted in full under Owner's earnings above. The scored base is TTM OE/share -$2.59; the normalized median is -$2.34, so the pin is also the more conservative choice, and the tier is F on either base.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 3.5%/yr): confirmed in the filed counts and the SBC trend — diluted shares 53,885,000 (FY2022) → 56,885,000 (FY2023) → 58,016,000 (FY2024) → 59,808,000 (FY2025) → 61,726,000 TTM (ttm.py); the FY2022→FY2025 window is the one the engine's 3.54%/yr share CAGR is computed on — while SBC rose $30,278,000 → $50,925,000 → $64,459,000 → $66,468,000 TTM. The -3.54% growth adjustment in the blend (key_numbers.md) is earned, not conservative padding; dilution is a real, ongoing cost of funding the losses.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): the recurring structural driver is the non-cash addbacks — SBC and D&A are added back to net income in the cash-flow statement, while this screen deducts SBC in full below OCF; that is precisely why the OCF-based conservative OE is the right series here, and it is still deeply negative. FY2025: net income -$77,670,000 vs OCF -$47,628,000, with SBC of $64,459,000 and D&A of $24,853,000 (financials_history.csv) added back, partly offset by working-capital and other operating outflows; FY2023 shows the same pattern (net income -$204,618,000 vs OCF -$142,474,000; SBC $30,278,000, D&A $29,310,000). FY2024 does not fully reconcile from the committed statement data: the gap is $144,632,000 (net income -$208,726,000 vs OCF -$64,094,000); the itemized addbacks in statements.json identify SBC $50,925,000 + D&A $31,432,000 = $82,357,000 of it, with other non-cash items of -$994,000 and itemized working-capital outflows of -$28,235,000 (receivables -$8,444,000, inventory -$7,986,000, payables -$11,805,000) — so the itemized lines net to $53,128,000, leaving roughly $91.5M of the bridge in cash-flow lines that statements.json does not itemize, which cannot be verified from the committed files; no tax deposit or impairment is visible in the lines that are itemized. The residual sits entirely inside the NI→OCF bridge: the scored OE is built from the filed OCF leg directly (OCF − capex − SBC), so it does not touch the base or the tier.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (2018, 2019): those two history years use the outstanding count recorded in the shares_tag column of financials_history.csv (FALLBACK:CommonStockSharesOutstanding), so pre-2020 per-share history is approximate. Both years sit far outside the last-3-FY base window; the sign and the tier are unaffected.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN from the engine): stated from the filing instead — at FY2025 Twist carried no filed funded borrowings (the last filed debt was $0 in FY2022 and small balances before that, per financials_history.csv); the balance sheet is equity-funded: cash $183,049,000 + short-term investments $49,385,000 against total liabilities of $168,903,000, of which operating lease liabilities are $75,572,000 and current liabilities $91,406,000 (fundamentals.json), with book equity of $472,958,000. Leverage is not the risk here; cash burn against that liquidity is.
